$schema.description: Optional path/URL of the JSON schema (ignored by the engine).

variables.description: Initial variables. Can be overridden at run time (`--var name=value`).

variable_types.description: Optional type of each variable (used by the editor and for validation).

triggers.description:
What starts the flow automatically while `autoflow watch` runs: new files in a folder,
new e-mail. Each event runs the flow once with the file / mail in a variable.

Settings.description:
Run-wide timing and safety settings (the PyAutoGUI `PAUSE` / `FAILSAFE`
equivalents). Command-line flags can override them for one run.

key_delay_ms.description:
Delay between keystrokes in ms for type_text and repeated key_press.
Raise it (150-250) for slow applications such as Tally.

input_pause_ms.description: Pause after every mouse/keyboard action in ms (like PyAutoGUI's PAUSE).

step_delay_ms.description:
Pause after every action step, in ms. Not added after if / loops / try themselves:
the steps inside them already get it.

mouse_move_ms.description: Default duration of mouse movements in ms (0 = jump instantly).

failsafe.description: Abort the run when the mouse is pushed into any screen corner (like PyAutoGUI's FAILSAFE).

abort_hotkey.description: Key combination that aborts the run at any time, e.g. `ctrl+alt+q`. Empty = none.

VarType.description:
Type of a flow variable. Values are stored as plain JSON in `variables`;
the type tells the editor which input to show and lets `validate` check the value.

oneOf.description: Any text (may contain ${other} variables).
Whole number.
Decimal number.
true / false.
Date as YYYY-MM-DD.
Time as HH:MM or HH:MM:SS (24 h).
Date and time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS].
Web address.
Path of a file.
Path of a folder.
JSON array, e.g. ["a", "b"].
A new (or changed) file in a folder.
New unread e-mail (IMAP or Outlook).

folder.description: Folder to watch (relative paths are relative to the flow's folder).

variable.description: Variable that receives the file's full path when the flow runs.

include_existing.description: Also run for files that are already there when watching starts.

settle_ms.description: Wait until the file has not changed for this long (it may still be copying).

move_to.description: After a successful run, move the file into this folder (e.g. "done"); empty = leave it.

move_failed_to.description: After a failed run, move the file into this folder (e.g. "failed"); empty = leave it.

source.description: "imap" (Gmail, Zoho, any IMAP server) or "outlook" (the Outlook desktop app).

provider.description: IMAP: a provider from File > Settings > E-mail providers, or custom with imap_host.

username.description: IMAP login, usually the e-mail address.

password_secret.description: Name of the password stored with `autoflow secret set NAME` (Gmail: an App Password).

folder.description: Folder to watch (IMAP: INBOX; Outlook: Inbox or Inbox/Sub).

from.description: Only mail from this sender (address or part of it).

subject_contains.description: Only mail whose subject contains this text.

save_attachments_to.description: Save attachments here (each mail's saved paths are in mail.attachments).

attachment_filter.description: Only attachments matching this pattern, e.g. *.pdf.

move_to.description: Move handled mail to this folder afterwards (it is always marked read).

variable.description: Variable that receives the mail record {from, subject, date, body, attachments, ...}.

Step.description:
One step of a flow: common settings plus the action (`"action": "..."`)
and the action's own fields, all at the same JSON level.

id.description: Unique id within the flow, used in logs.

comment.description: Free-text note shown in the editor.

on_error.description: What to do when the step fails after all retries.

delay_before_ms.description: Wait this many ms before the step runs.

delay_after_ms.description:
Wait this many ms after the step succeeds (in addition to settings.step_delay_ms).
Ignored on if / loops / try; put it on the last step inside instead.

oneOf.description: Set a variable (strings are interpolated).
Add a number to a numeric variable (counters).
Write a message to the run log.
Pause for a number of milliseconds.
Run `then` steps if the condition holds, otherwise `else` steps.
Run `steps` a fixed number of times.
Run `steps` while the condition holds (bounded by max_iterations).
Run `steps` once per item of a list.
Leave the innermost repeat / while / for_each loop.
End the flow now, successfully or as a failure.
Run another flow file as a sub-flow.
Run steps; on failure run `catch` instead of stopping; always run `finally`.
Copy a file (to a file path or into a folder).
Move or rename a file or folder.
Delete file(s); wildcards allowed.
Write or append text to a file (creates folders).
Read a text file into a variable.
Store "true"/"false" depending on whether a path exists.
Store name, extension, size, dates etc. of a path in an object variable.
Create a folder (and parents).
Delete a folder.
List files/folders matching a pattern into an array variable.
Read a sheet (or one column) of an Excel workbook into a list variable.
Read a CSV/TSV table (or one column) into a list variable.
Read the text of a PDF (all or some pages) into a variable.
Add a value or record to a list variable (collect results).
Write a list of records to a CSV file (Excel-friendly).
Write a list of records to a new Excel workbook.
Read a table from a PDF (invoice lines, statements) into records.
Read the text and tables of a Word .docx file.
Make a .docx from a template, replacing {{placeholders}} (letters, certificates).
Create a simple .docx report: title, paragraphs and a table.
Put files and folders into a .zip.
Unpack a .zip (all files or those matching a pattern).
Trim, change case, count or URL-encode text.
Replace text (plain or regular expression).
Pick out text with a regular expression (first match or all).
Split text into a list (by comma, line, tab or pattern).
Join a list into one text.
(Beta) Redact personal data (PAN, Aadhaar, mobile, names, DOB, patient details, your own patterns) in a folder of PDF, Word, Excel, picture and text files, offline.
(Beta) Redact personal data in a text (Indian DPDP identifiers, labelled details, your own patterns).
(Beta) Replace IDs (account numbers, PAN, mobile...) with tokens that only your key can turn back; originals kept encrypted in a vault.
(Beta) Turn tokens made by pseudonymize back into the original values (needs the vault and the key).
Format, add to, subtract or compare dates.
Evaluate arithmetic such as ${amount} * 18 / 100.
Run a SELECT on SQLite or any ODBC database (SQL Server, MySQL, Access, Tally) into a list of records.
Run INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / CREATE on SQLite or an ODBC database.
Call a web API or download a file (GET/POST/...).
Ask a local (LM Studio, Ollama) or cloud (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude) AI model; optionally force one of given labels.
Start a program, optionally waiting and capturing its output.
Terminate all processes with the given image name.
Open a file, folder or URL with its default application.
Wait for a window and bring it to the foreground.
Wait until a window with the given title exists.
Wait until no window with the given title exists.
Close a window (like clicking X).
Maximize, minimize or restore a window.
Store "true"/"false" depending on whether a window exists (no waiting).
Move the mouse pointer.
Click (optionally at a position).
Scroll the mouse wheel.
Drag from one point to another.
Press and hold a mouse button.
Release a held mouse button.
Store the current pointer position.
Type text into the focused control.
Press a key or key combination such as ctrl+s.
Press and hold key(s), e.g. shift while clicking.
Release key(s) held with key_down.
Find a UI element (UI Automation) and click it.
Find an input element and set its text.
Read an element's value/text into a variable.
Wait until a UI element exists.
Store "true"/"false" depending on whether an element exists (waits up to timeout_ms).
Put text on the clipboard.
Read clipboard text into a variable.
Save a PNG screenshot of a monitor, window or region.
Store the primary screen width and height.
Store the colour of a screen pixel as #RRGGBB.
Store "true"/"false": does a pixel have the expected colour?
Look for a picture on screen; store found/x/y (never fails).
Store every place a picture appears on screen.
Wait for a picture on screen and click it.
Wait until a picture appears on screen.
Wait until a picture is no longer on screen.
Read the text on screen, in a window or in a picture (Windows OCR, offline).
Look for text on screen; store found/x/y (never fails).
Wait for text on screen and click it (e.g. a button or menu without UI Automation).
Start Edge/Chrome and open a page (URL or local .html file).
Load another page in the open browser.
Type text into a page element given by id or selector.
Click a page element given by id or selector.
Wait until a page element exists.
Wait until some text appears on the page (e.g. after a search).
Read a page element's text, value or attribute into a variable.
Save a PNG of the page or of one element.
Run JavaScript in the page and store the result.
Close the browser.
Send an e-mail with attachments through SMTP (Gmail, Microsoft 365, any server).
Create an e-mail in the Outlook desktop app and send it (or show it as a draft).
Read messages from an IMAP mailbox (Gmail...) and save their attachments.
Read messages from an Outlook desktop folder and save their attachments.
Show a message box and store which button was clicked.
Ask the user to type a value (optionally masked).

OnError.description: Error handling policy for a step.

oneOf.description: Abort the whole flow (default).
Log the error and continue with the next step.

value.description:
Value. Strings are interpolated; a string that is exactly `${x}` copies
x's value as-is (lists stay lists). Numbers, bools, arrays and objects are stored as given.

Int.description: An integer, or a string containing `${variables}` that evaluates to one.

Condition.description:
`left <op> right`, both sides interpolated. Numeric comparison is used when
both sides parse as numbers, otherwise text (case-sensitive unless `ignore_case`).

right.description: Right-hand value (ignored by is_empty, not_empty, is_true, is_false, path_exists).

oneOf.description: `left` is empty (`right` ignored).
`left` is not empty (`right` ignored).
`left` is "true", "yes" or "1" (`right` ignored).
`left` is "false", "no", "0" or empty (`right` ignored).
A file or folder exists at path `left` (`right` ignored).
`left` matches regex-free wildcard pattern `right` (`*` and `?`).

then.description: Steps run when the condition is true.

else.description: Steps run when the condition is false.

condition.description: Loop while this is true (checked before each iteration).

max_iterations.description: Safety limit; the step fails when reached.

items.description:
A JSON array, or a string: `${list_var}` (an array variable) or text
that is split into lines.

success.description: true = finish the flow successfully, false = fail it.

path.description: Path of another flow JSON file (relative paths resolve against this flow's folder).

variables.description: Variables passed to the sub-flow (values interpolated).

share_variables.description: If true, variables set by the sub-flow are copied back into this flow.

Try.description: Run steps; if one fails, run `catch` instead of stopping the flow; always run `finally`.

catch.description: Steps run when one of `steps` fails (the error text is in error_var).

finally.description: Steps run afterwards in every case (e.g. close the browser or the program).

error_var.description: Variable receiving the error message (it names the step that failed).

source.description: File (or folder for file_move) to copy/move; wildcards allowed (`C:\in\*.csv`).

destination.description: Destination file path, or a folder: an existing folder, or any path ending in `\` (created if missing).

overwrite.description: Replace existing files instead of failing.

path.description: File path; may contain wildcards (`C:\tmp\*.log`).

missing_ok.description: Do not fail when nothing matches.

path.description: File to write; parent folders are created.

content.description: Text to write (interpolated). Use ${newline} for line breaks.

path.description: File path (relative paths resolve against the flow folder).

output_var.description: Variable that receives the result.

path.description: File or folder path.

output_var.description: Receives {name, stem, extension, parent, size, is_dir, exists, modified}.

path.description: Folder path (relative paths resolve against the flow folder).
Folder to delete.

recursive.description: Delete contents too. Without it only empty folders are removed.

missing_ok.description: Do not fail when the folder does not exist.

path.description: Folder to list.

output_var.description: Receives an array of full paths, sorted.

path.description: Workbook file (.xlsx, .xlsm, .xls, .xlsb, .ods).

sheet.description: Sheet name; empty = the first sheet.

range.description: Only this cell range, e.g. `A1:D50`; empty = the whole used area.

has_header.description: The first row holds column names.

column.description: Return only this column as a list: header name (e.g. `GSTIN`), letter (`B`) or number (`2`). Empty = all columns.

skip_empty.description: Leave out empty rows (and empty cells when reading one column).

output_var.description: Variable receiving the data: a list of values (column), of records {header: value}, or of rows.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows (optional).

path.description: CSV / TSV / text table file.

delimiter.description: Separator character: `,` `;` `|` or `tab`; empty = detect automatically.

has_header.description: The first row holds column names.

column.description: Return only this column as a list: header name, letter (`B`) or number (`2`). Empty = all columns.

skip_empty.description: Leave out empty rows (and empty cells when reading one column).

output_var.description: Variable receiving the data: a list of values (column), of records {header: value}, or of rows.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows (optional).

path.description: PDF file.

pages.description: Pages to read, e.g. `1`, `2-4`, `1,3,5-`; empty = all pages.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the text (pages separated by a blank line).

page_count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of pages in the PDF (optional).

stream_order.description:
Keep the order the text is stored in the PDF instead of reading it line by line from the
top of the page. Try this for newspaper-style pages with several text columns.

ListAppend.description: Append a value (text, number or record) to a list variable, creating it if needed.

name.description: List variable to add to (missing = a new empty list).

value.description:
Value to add. Strings are interpolated; an object such as
{"Comment": "${row.Comment}", "Label": "${label}"} adds a record (a row for write_csv / write_excel).

path.description: CSV file to write (folders are created).

data.description: The rows: usually "${results}" - a list of records, a list of lists or a list of values.

columns.description: Columns to write, in order (empty = every key of the records, in first-seen order).

header.description: Write a header row with the column names.

append.description: Add to the end of an existing file (the header is not repeated).

excel_bom.description: Start the file with a UTF-8 marker so Excel shows non-English text correctly.

escape_formulas.description:
Put a ' before text starting with = + - @ so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of
running it as a formula. Use for data from e-mail, web pages or AI replies that is opened in Excel.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows written (optional).

path.description: .xlsx workbook to create (an existing file is replaced; close it in Excel first).

data.description:
The rows: usually "${results}" - a list of records, a list of lists or a list of values.
Numbers stay numbers; text stays text (see allow_formulas).

columns.description: Columns to write, in order (empty = every key of the records, in first-seen order).

header.description: Write a bold, frozen header row with the column names.

autofit.description: Size the columns to fit their contents.

allow_formulas.description:
Write text starting with = as a live formula (e.g. "=SUM(B2:B9)"). Off by default, so text
from e-mail, web pages or AI replies can never run as a formula when the file is opened.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows written (optional).

path.description: The PDF to read. It must contain text (a scanned picture needs OCR: ocr_read with image).

min_columns.description: Keep only lines with at least this many cells; this drops headings and notes around the table.

gap.description:
Split cells where the space between words is wider than this many times the font size
(0 = default 0.5). Raise it if cells are split in two; lower it if columns run together.

has_header.description: The first row holds the column names (rows become records).

column.description: Return only this column (name, letter or number) as a plain list.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the rows.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows (optional).

path.description: The .docx file to read (old .doc files: save them as .docx first).

output_var.description: Variable receiving the text, one paragraph per line.

tables_var.description: Variable receiving the tables: a list with one entry per table (optional).

has_header.description: Treat the first row of each table as column names, so rows become records.

template.description: The .docx template containing placeholders such as {{name}} and {{amount}}.

path.description: The .docx file to create (the template is not changed).

missing_ok.description: Leave placeholders that have no value as they are, instead of failing the step.

path.description: The .docx file to create (an existing one is replaced).

data.description: A table to add after the text, usually "${rows}" (optional).

columns.description: Columns of the table, in order (empty = every key of the records).

path.description: The .zip file to create (an existing one is replaced).

sources.description: Files and folders to put in it (wildcards allowed, e.g. "output/*.pdf"); folders keep their structure.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of files added (optional).

path.description: The .zip file to unpack.

destination.description: Folder to unpack into (empty = a folder named after the zip, next to it).

pattern.description: Only files matching this pattern, e.g. *.pdf (empty = everything).

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist (otherwise the step fails).

output_var.description: Variable receiving the list of unpacked file paths (optional).

operation.description:
trim, upper, lower, title (Each Word Capitalised), length (number of characters),
url_encode (for a URL query value) or remove_spaces.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the result.

find.description: Text to look for (a regular expression when `regex` is true).

replace_with.description: Replacement. With regex, $1 / ${name} insert captured groups.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the result.

group.description: Capture group to return: 0 = the whole match, 1 = the first ( ) group...

all.description: Return every match as a list instead of the first one.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the match ("" when nothing matches) or the list of matches.

separator.description: Separator, e.g. "," or "\n" for lines or "\t" for tabs (a regular expression when `regex` is true).

regex.description: Treat `separator` as a regular expression, e.g. "[,;]\\s*".

output_var.description: Variable receiving the list of parts.

separator.description: Put between the items, e.g. ", " or "\n".

output_var.description: Variable receiving the text.

oneOf.description: The kind in brackets: [PAN], [MOBILE], [NAME]...
Every letter and digit becomes X; spaces and dashes stay (XXXXX XXXXX).
Like mask, but the last 4 letters/digits stay visible (XXXXXXXX1234), handy for audit trails.
The text given in `replace_with`.

OcrMode.description: When PDFs and pictures are read with OCR.

oneOf.description: Text PDFs use their own text; pages without text (scans) are read with OCR.
Also OCR pages that have text (catches pictures of text inside text PDFs; slower).
Never OCR: scanned pages and pictures are left unredacted (and reported).

input.description: A file, or a folder of documents to redact. The originals are never changed.

output.description:
Where the redacted copies go: a folder (the input's sub-folders are kept), or a file name
when input is one file. Must not be the input.

include.description:
Which files, e.g. "*.pdf;*.docx" (empty = every supported file: PDF, Word .docx, Excel
.xlsx, pictures, text, CSV, JSON, XML, HTML).

rules.description:
Built-in rules to use (empty = all): pan, aadhaar, mobile, email, bank_account, ifsc, card,
upi, passport, voter_id, driving_licence, dob, age, gender, name, patient_id, health,
address, pincode. "none" = only your own patterns and words.

patterns.description:
Your own regular expressions, by label, e.g. {"EMPLOYEE_ID": "EMP-\\d{5}"}. To redact only
part of a match, name that part `value`: {"POLICY": "Policy No:\\s*(?P<value>\\S+)"}.

words.description: Words or names to redact wherever they appear (whole words, any case).

words_file.description: A text or CSV file with more words or names, one per line (first column).

mask_style.description:
label = [PAN], mask = XXXXXXXXXX, partial = XXXXXX234F (last 4 kept), text = replace_with.
PDFs and pictures always get black boxes.

replace_with.description: The replacement when mask_style is text, e.g. "***".

strict.description: Check the Aadhaar (Verhoeff) and card (Luhn) checksums, so other long numbers are left alone.

ocr.description:
auto = scanned pages and pictures are read with Windows OCR; always = OCR every PDF page
too (finds text inside pictures; slower); never = no OCR.

ocr_language.description: OCR language tag such as en-US (empty = the Windows display languages).

ocr_rotated.description:
Also read text turned sideways or upside down (landscape scans, rotated ID cards). OCR
takes four passes, so it is slower; turn off only for upright documents.

pdf_dpi.description: Resolution of the redacted PDF pages in dots per inch (150 is clear and compact; 200-300 for small print).

clear_metadata.description:
Word and Excel: clear the author and "last saved by" fields and redact the document
properties (title, subject, keywords, comments, custom properties). PDFs and pictures are
rebuilt from pixels, so they keep no metadata at all.

overwrite.description: Redo files that are already in the output folder.

threads.description: Files worked on at the same time (0 = automatic).

report.description: A CSV report: one line per file with what was found (counts only, never the values).

continue_on_problems.description:
Let the flow go on when some files failed or could not be checked (unverified), or when the
output folder holds files this redaction did not make (foreign). Off by default: the step
then fails, so later steps (zip, e-mail, upload) never send a folder that is not completely
redacted. The report and summary are written either way.

rules.description:
Built-in rules to use (empty = all): pan, aadhaar, mobile, email, bank_account, ifsc, card,
upi, passport, voter_id, driving_licence, dob, age, gender, name, patient_id, health,
address, pincode. "none" = only your own patterns and words.

patterns.description:
Your own regular expressions, by label, e.g. {"EMPLOYEE_ID": "EMP-\\d{5}"}. To redact only
part of a match, name that part `value`: {"POLICY": "Policy No:\\s*(?P<value>\\S+)"}.
Start with (?i) to ignore upper/lower case.

words.description: Words or names to redact wherever they appear (whole words, any case).

words_file.description: A text or CSV file with more words or names, one per line (first column).

mask_style.description: label = [PAN], mask = XXXXXXXXXX, partial = XXXXXX234F (last 4 kept), text = replace_with.

replace_with.description: The replacement when mask_style is text, e.g. "***".

strict.description:
Check the Aadhaar (Verhoeff) and card (Luhn) checksums, so other 12-16 digit numbers
(order numbers, phone bills) are left alone.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the cleaned text.

report_var.description: Variable receiving what was found, e.g. {"PAN": 1, "MOBILE": 2} (optional).

input.description: One value to replace (interpolated), e.g. "${row.AccountNo}". Leave empty when using data.

data.description: Or a whole table: a list of records such as "${rows}" (from read_excel / read_csv).

columns.description: With data: the columns to replace, e.g. ["AccountNo", "PAN"] (the other columns stay).

prefix.description: Text in front of every token, e.g. "ACC-" gives ACC-7K2M9QX4T1B3HC0D.

domain.description:
Keeps purposes apart: the same value gets different tokens in different domains. Use one per
purpose and kind, e.g. "vendor_share_2026:account", so tables shared for different purposes
can't be linked. Empty = one shared domain (the validator warns).

normalize.description:
Remove spaces and dashes and use capitals before making the token, so "1234 5678" and
"12345678" get the same token (the vault keeps the tidied value).

vault.description: The vault file keeping the original values, encrypted (a SQLite file).

key_secret.description:
Name of the key in Windows Credential Manager. Created on first use; back it up, without
it the vault cannot be read.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the token (with input) or the new table (with data).

count_var.description: Variable receiving how many values were replaced (optional).

UnknownToken.description: What to do with a value the vault doesn't know.

oneOf.description: Leave it as it is (and count it in the log).
Make it empty.
Stop the step with an error.

input.description: One token to turn back (interpolated), e.g. "${row.AccountNo}". Leave empty when using data.

data.description: Or a whole table: a list of records such as "${rows}".

columns.description: With data: the columns holding tokens, e.g. ["AccountNo"].

vault.description: The vault file made by pseudonymize.

key_secret.description: Name of the key in Windows Credential Manager (the same as when the tokens were made).

unknown.description: keep = leave unknown values as they are, empty = blank them, fail = stop with an error.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the original value (with input) or the restored table (with data).

count_var.description: Variable receiving how many values were restored (optional).

oneOf.description: Re-write the date in `format`.
Add `amount` `unit`s (negative to subtract), then format.
Whole `unit`s from `date` to `other_date` (a number).
An object with year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday (1 = Monday), weekday_name, month_name, day_of_year.

date.description: The date (interpolated); empty = now, "today" = today 00:00. Excel date numbers work too.

input_format.description: How `date` is written, e.g. dd/MM/yyyy (empty = recognise common formats, day first).

amount.description: add: how many units (negative to go back).

unit.description: add / diff: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months or years.

format.description: Output format (tokens as in ${now:...}): yyyy MM dd HH hh mm ss tt MMM dddd.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the result.

expression.description:
Expression (interpolated), e.g. "${amount} * 18 / 100". Supports + - * / % ^ ( ),
comparisons (result 1 or 0) and round(x), round(0.01, x), int, floor, ceil, abs, min, max, sqrt.

decimals.description: Round the result to this many decimal places (empty = no rounding).

output_var.description: Variable receiving the number.

DbQuery.description: Where the data is. See the db_query description for connection examples.

connection.description:
A SQLite file (sqlite:data/app.db, or a path ending in .db) or an ODBC connection string, e.g.
DSN=TallyODBC64_9000 or Driver={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};Server=.;Database=Sales;Trusted_Connection=yes;TrustServerCertificate=yes.
Write {password} where the password goes; it is taken from password_secret.

password_secret.description: Name of the database password stored with `autoflow secret set NAME` (replaces {password}).

sql.description: SELECT statement. Use ? for values and list them in params, e.g. "SELECT * FROM Ledger WHERE Parent = ?".

params.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order (interpolated), e.g. ["${group}"].

max_rows.description: Return at most this many rows (0 = all).

output_var.description: Variable receiving the rows as a list of records {column: value}.

count_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows (optional).

DbExecute.description: Where the data is. See the db_query description for connection examples.

connection.description:
A SQLite file (sqlite:data/app.db, or a path ending in .db) or an ODBC connection string, e.g.
DSN=TallyODBC64_9000 or Driver={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};Server=.;Database=Sales;Trusted_Connection=yes;TrustServerCertificate=yes.
Write {password} where the password goes; it is taken from password_secret.

password_secret.description: Name of the database password stored with `autoflow secret set NAME` (replaces {password}).

sql.description:
INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / CREATE statement with ? placeholders, e.g.
"INSERT INTO Labels (Comment, Label) VALUES (?, ?)". Without params, SQLite runs a whole script.

params.description: Values for the ? placeholders, in order (interpolated), e.g. ["${row.Comment}", "${label}"].

affected_var.description: Variable receiving the number of rows changed (optional).

method.description: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or HEAD.

headers.description: Extra request headers, e.g. {"Accept": "application/json"} (values are interpolated).

body.description: Request body. A string is sent as-is; an object or list is sent as JSON.

bearer_secret.description: Name of a token stored with `autoflow secret set NAME`, sent as "Authorization: Bearer <token>" (optional).

save_to.description: Save the response body to this file (for downloads); output_var then receives the path.

fail_on_error_status.description: Fail the step when the server answers with an error status (400 and above).

parse_json.description: Store a JSON response as an object/list (so ${response.field} works) instead of text.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the whole request, in ms.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the response body.

status_var.description: Variable receiving the HTTP status code (optional).

AiPrompt.description: Send one prompt to a language model and store its reply.

provider.description:
A provider from File > Settings > AI providers: lmstudio (local, default), ollama (local),
openai, gemini, anthropic, openai_compatible (+ base_url), or one you added. Empty fields
below use the provider's server, default model and key name.

model.description: Model name. Empty = the model loaded in LM Studio/Ollama, or a default for cloud providers.

base_url.description: Server address; empty = the provider's default (LM Studio: http://localhost:1234/v1).

api_key_secret.description: Name of the API key stored with `autoflow secret set NAME` (not needed for local servers).

system.description: Instructions for the model (interpolated), e.g. "You classify customer comments."

labels.description:
Allowed answers, e.g. ["Fav", "UnFav", "Neutral"]. The model is told to reply with one,
and the stored value is always exactly one of them (the step fails otherwise).

json.description: Ask for JSON and store the parsed object (so ${reply.field} works).

temperature.description: Randomness, 0 = most predictable (empty = provider default; ignored by Claude).

max_tokens.description: Longest reply, in tokens (thinking models need room to think).

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the reply, in ms.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the reply (or the label / parsed JSON).

program.description: Executable path or name on PATH (e.g. `notepad.exe`).

wait.description: Wait for the program to exit.

timeout_ms.description: When waiting: fail after this many ms (0 = no limit).

output_var.description: When waiting: variable receiving stdout.

exit_code_var.description: When waiting: variable receiving the exit code.

check_exit_code.description: When waiting: fail if the exit code is not 0.

missing_ok.description: Do not fail when no such process is running.

target.description: File, folder or URL to open with its default application.

title.description:
Window title; matches when the title contains this text (case-insensitive)
unless `exact` is true.

exact.description: Require the whole title to match exactly.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the window, in ms.

title.description:
Window title; matches when the title contains this text (case-insensitive)
unless `exact` is true.

exact.description: Require the whole title to match exactly.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the window, in ms.

title.description:
Window title; matches when the title contains this text (case-insensitive)
unless `exact` is true.

exact.description: Require the whole title to match exactly.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the window, in ms.

output_var.description: Variable that receives "true" or "false".

Tween.description: Easing curve for mouse movement (PyAutoGUI "tween" functions).

x.description: Screen X in pixels (or offset when relative).

y.description: Screen Y in pixels (or offset when relative).

relative.description: Move relative to the current position (PyAutoGUI moveRel).

duration_ms.description: Movement time in ms; null = settings.mouse_move_ms (0 = instant).

x.description: Screen X; omit (null) to click at the current position.

y.description: Screen Y; omit (null) to click at the current position.

clicks.description: 1 = single click, 2 = double click, 3 = triple click.

duration_ms.description: Time to move to (x, y) in ms; null = settings.mouse_move_ms.

amount.description: Wheel notches; positive = down/right, negative = up/left.

horizontal.description: Scroll sideways instead of up/down (PyAutoGUI hscroll).

x.description: Screen X to scroll at; null = current position.

y.description: Screen Y to scroll at; null = current position.

relative.description: Treat to_x/to_y as offsets from the start (PyAutoGUI dragRel).

duration_ms.description: Drag time in ms (some apps need a slow drag to register it).

MouseButtonAt.description: Press (mouse_down) or release (mouse_up) a button, optionally at a position.

oneOf.description: Press real keys per character (most compatible; default).
Inject Unicode characters (any language, but some apps drop them).
Paste through the clipboard (fast for long text; clipboard is restored).

text.description: Text to type (interpolated). `\n` presses Enter, `\t` presses Tab.

delay_ms.description: Delay between keystrokes in ms; null = settings.key_delay_ms.

mode.description: keys (default, most compatible), unicode, or paste (via clipboard).

times.description: How many times to press it.

interval_ms.description: Pause between presses in ms; null = settings.key_delay_ms.

KeyHold.description:
Hold (key_down) or release (key_up) keys, e.g. `shift` or `ctrl+alt`.
Keys still held at the end of the run are released automatically.

keys.description: Key or combination; key_down presses left to right, key_up releases right to left.

UiClick.description:
Finds a UI element through Windows UI Automation. At least one of
`name`, `automation_id`, `class_name`, `control_type` should be set.
Use `autoflow inspect` (or the GUI "Pick" button) to discover them.

window.description: Restrict the search to the top-level window whose title contains this.

name.description: Element name (the text a screen reader would say).

name_contains.description: Match when the name contains `name` instead of equalling it.

automation_id.description: UIA AutomationId (most stable; prefer it when present).

timeout_ms.description: How long to keep searching, in ms.

invoke.description: Prefer the UIA Invoke pattern (works on hidden/covered controls) and fall back to a real mouse click.

path.description: PNG path to write.

window.description: Capture only the window whose title contains this text.

region.description: Capture only this screen rectangle {x, y, width, height}; null = whole monitor.

width_var.description: Variable receiving the primary screen width.

height_var.description: Variable receiving the primary screen height.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the colour as `#RRGGBB`.

ImageFind.description:
Locate a picture on screen (PyAutoGUI locateOnScreen). The match is
tolerant to small rendering differences through `confidence`.

image.description:
PNG/JPG file of what to look for (relative paths resolve against the flow folder).
Capture it with Studio's "Snip image" button or Win+Shift+S.

confidence.description: Required similarity 0.0-1.0 (1.0 = pixel-perfect). 0.9 suits most UI.

region.description: Search only this screen rectangle (much faster); null = all monitors.

timeout_ms.description: Keep searching for up to this many ms.

found_var.description: Variable receiving "true"/"false" (the step never fails when not found).

x_var.description: Variable receiving the centre X of the match.

y_var.description: Variable receiving the centre Y of the match.

region.description: Search only this screen rectangle (much faster); null = all monitors.

timeout_ms.description: Keep searching for up to this many ms.

output_var.description: Variable receiving an array of matches [{x, y, left, top, width, height, score}].

OcrRead.description: Where OCR reads from: an image file, a window, a screen region or a monitor.

image.description: Read this picture file (PNG/JPG/BMP) instead of the screen.

window.description: Read this window (part of its title), e.g. "Tally" or "Notepad".

region.description: Read only this screen rectangle {x, y, width, height}; null = whole window / monitor.

monitor.description: Monitor to read when no window or region is given (0 = primary).

language.description: Language tag such as en-US or hi (empty = the Windows display languages).

scale.description: Enlarge the picture before reading; 2 helps with small screen fonts.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the recognised text (one line per text line).

lines_var.description: Variable receiving the list of lines (optional).

words_var.description: Variable receiving every word with its screen position: {text, x, y, width, height, center_x, center_y} (optional).

OcrFind.description: Where OCR reads from: an image file, a window, a screen region or a monitor.

image.description: Read this picture file (PNG/JPG/BMP) instead of the screen.

window.description: Read this window (part of its title), e.g. "Tally" or "Notepad".

region.description: Read only this screen rectangle {x, y, width, height}; null = whole window / monitor.

monitor.description: Monitor to read when no window or region is given (0 = primary).

language.description: Language tag such as en-US or hi (empty = the Windows display languages).

scale.description: Enlarge the picture before reading; 2 helps with small screen fonts.

text.description: Text to look for (interpolated); may be several words, e.g. "Save As".

occurrence.description: Which match to use when the text appears more than once (1 = first, top to bottom).

timeout_ms.description: Keep looking for up to this many ms (the screen may still be changing).

found_var.description: Variable receiving "true"/"false" (ocr_find never fails when the text is missing).

x_var.description: Variable receiving the centre X of the text on screen.

y_var.description: Variable receiving the centre Y of the text on screen.

offset_x.description: Click this many pixels right of the text centre (negative = left), e.g. into the box next to a label.

offset_y.description: Click this many pixels below the text centre (negative = above).

url.description: Page to open: a URL (https://…) or a local .html file path.

browser.description: "edge" (default), "chrome", or the full path to a Chromium-based browser .exe.

keep_open.description: Leave the browser open when the flow ends.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the page to load, in ms.

url.description: URL or local .html file path to load in the open browser.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the page to load, in ms.

BrowserType.description: Which element on the page: by `element_id` (simplest) or by CSS `selector`.

element_id.description:
The element's id attribute, e.g. `email` for <input id="email"> (without #).
(Named element_id because every step already has its own `id`.)

selector.description: CSS selector instead of an id, e.g. `form button[type=submit]`, `.result`.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the element to appear, in ms.

press_enter.description: Press Enter after typing (submits most forms).

BrowserElement.description: Which element on the page: by `element_id` (simplest) or by CSS `selector`.

element_id.description:
The element's id attribute, e.g. `email` for <input id="email"> (without #).
(Named element_id because every step already has its own `id`.)

selector.description: CSS selector instead of an id, e.g. `form button[type=submit]`, `.result`.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the element to appear, in ms.

text.description: Text to wait for (interpolated), e.g. a heading that only the result page shows.

element_id.description: Look only inside this element (by id); empty = the whole page.

selector.description: Look only inside this element (by CSS selector); empty = the whole page.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in ms.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the page/element text once found (optional).

BrowserGetText.description: Which element on the page: by `element_id` (simplest) or by CSS `selector`.

element_id.description:
The element's id attribute, e.g. `email` for <input id="email"> (without #).
(Named element_id because every step already has its own `id`.)

selector.description: CSS selector instead of an id, e.g. `form button[type=submit]`, `.result`.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the element to appear, in ms.

attribute.description: What to read: empty = visible text, `value` = input value, `html`, or any attribute name (e.g. `href`).

output_var.description: Variable that receives the result.

path.description: PNG path to write.

element_id.description: Only this element (by its id attribute); empty = the visible page.

selector.description: Only this element (by CSS selector); empty = the visible page.

full_page.description: Capture the whole page including the parts below the fold (ignored for an element).

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the element, in ms.

script.description: JavaScript expression evaluated in the page; its value is returned (promises are awaited).

output_var.description: Variable that receives the result.

provider.description:
A provider from File > Settings > E-mail providers (gmail, outlook365, outlook.com, yahoo,
zoho, or one you added; fills server and port), or custom.

username.description: Login name, usually your e-mail address. Empty = no login (internal relays).

password_secret.description:
Name of the password stored in Windows Credential Manager (`autoflow secret set NAME`).
For Gmail use an App Password. Never put the password itself in the flow.

from.description: Sender, e.g. `Accounts <me@gmail.com>`; empty = the user name.

attachments.description: Files to attach, one per item (interpolated; relative to the flow folder).

timeout_ms.description: Give up after this many ms.

attachments.description: Files to attach, one per item (interpolated; relative to the flow folder).

send_now.description: Send immediately. Off = open the mail in Outlook as a draft for you to check and send.

account.description: Send from this Outlook account (its e-mail address); empty = the default account.

ReadEmail.description: Read e-mail from an IMAP mailbox (Gmail, Zoho, Yahoo, any IMAP server).

provider.description:
A provider from File > Settings > E-mail providers (gmail, outlook365, yahoo, zoho, zoho.in,
or one you added), or custom (then set imap_host).

username.description: Mailbox login, usually the e-mail address.

password_secret.description: Name of the password stored with `autoflow secret set NAME` (Gmail: an App Password).

folder.description: Folder to read, e.g. INBOX (IMAP) or Inbox/Invoices (Outlook).

from.description: Only messages from this sender (address or part of it).

subject_contains.description: Only messages whose subject contains this text.

since.description: Only messages received on or after this date (e.g. 01-11-2026, "today"; empty = any date).

max.description: Read at most this many messages.

move_to.description: Move the messages to this folder afterwards (e.g. Processed); empty = leave them.

save_attachments_to.description: Save attachments into this folder (empty = only list their names).

attachment_filter.description: Only attachments matching this pattern, e.g. *.pdf or *.xlsx.

output_var.description:
Variable receiving the list of messages:
{from, from_name, to, subject, date, body, attachments (saved paths), attachment_names}.

count_var.description: Variable receiving how many messages were read (optional).

MessageBox.description: A message box (PyAutoGUI alert / confirm). Blocks until the user answers.

buttons.description: ok, ok_cancel, yes_no, yes_no_cancel or retry_cancel.

icon.description: info, warning, error, question or none.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the clicked button: ok, cancel, yes, no, retry.

InputBox.description: Ask the user to type a value (PyAutoGUI prompt / password).

prompt.description: Question shown above the text box (interpolated).

password.description: Mask the input (for passwords). The value is never written to the log.

image.description: Picture to show above the text box (PNG/JPG path), e.g. a CAPTCHA captured with browser_screenshot.

output_var.description: Variable receiving the text.

fail_on_cancel.description: Fail the step when the user presses Cancel (otherwise the variable is set to "").
